name: What type of drywall is best for a kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: What type of drywall is best for a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moisture-resistant drywall, commonly called green board, or purple board is standard for general kitchen walls near sinks and preparation areas. For areas directly behind cooking ranges or shared garage walls, local building codes often require Type X fire-rated drywall, which is 5/8-inch thick. If you plan to install heavy tile or marble backsplashes, cement backer board or specialized tile underlayment is preferred over standard drywall to handle moisture and weight. At HH Remodeling LLC, we evaluate your kitchen layout to match the correct drywall type to each wall section before hanging.
acceptedAnswer.description: Moisture-resistant drywall is best for standard kitchen walls, while fire-rated Type X is used near heat sources and cement backer board is required behind heavy tile backsplashes.
